Mira pulled her hand back slowly, watching droplets cling to her fingertips before evaporating into tiny wisps of prismatic steam. The steam curled upward, forming shapes that almost looked deliberate—a bird, a face, a door. She blinked, and they dissolved into nothing. Behind her, the bathroom mirror rippled unbidden, and she caught movement in its watery surface. Not her reflection—something else. A figure stood in a room that wasn't her bathroom, surrounded by shelves of books that seemed to breathe and shift. The figure turned, and Mira's breath caught. a rabbit who lived deep in the woods. They lived in a small town filled with all other sorts of woodland creatures. It was a peaceful place, but tensions lurked not far from the town. Paul was lonely although she had a couple of hundred siblings. One day, Paul decided to go and find some friends, somewhere else than the beach, which she knew. was THE place to go when trying to get friends. So Paul packed her shell with beach towels and sunscreen and headed off! On the way Paul noticed the expected amount of sick. But she was used to the smell. So she scooched on along the divide between forest and beach. Suddenly, a flash of light caught her eye - much like that of sun reflected . What was that? In the distance? Could it really be a creature undeterred by the foul, foul air that had filled the surroundings? Paul went closer to the palm tree. When she finally made it over there, there was nothing to be seen. Oh, well, time for a rest. She sat down for a while thinking about the flash of light she had seen. She had really hoped it could be a friend, but alas! It turned out to be yet another disappointment to add to the pile. She packed up her towel and started turning around, because she had to be home before sunset. As she turned, another flash of light caught her eye, this time it came from the heavens above! A great booming voice came from the skies and it seemed to Paul to tell her to "take a shower"? "A shower?" Paul thought. Then rain started pouring. "Oh great!" Paul shouted at the sky. At least she had her shell to keep her dry. But what was happening? It felt like her shell started rocking. The rain kept pouring down and she could hear the sound of the drops on her shell getting heavier and heavier. "What was that?" she said to herself. Her shell was melting! It poured down over her face and legs, and soon the shell was completely gone. She stood all alone and shell-less on the beach in the shell-melting rain. : A little shell-less naked tortoise alone in the rain. At first, Paul was confused. Then came the sadness - her home was gone. But then... came the feeling of burning. in her loins. A new sensation, a good sensation, a sensation making her feel more lonely than ever. CRASH! The loudest noise Paul had ever heard filled the air. She felt inspired to go on. She was ready to face the world! The loud sound filled Paul with passion and made her focused. She decided to go to the source of the everlasting friendships. She could see everything clearly now, and she knew that she had to find Ursula, the sea witch. In her cave, Paul would find the friends she yearned for. "I must go to the ocean!" thought Paul. She then collected all her remaining strength to do a backflip into the cold waters of the ocean. She felt the crash of the water against her naked back. Swimming was a lot easier without the heavy shell. At the bottom of the sea, she saw a cave surrounded by white sharks. This did not frighten her. Her will, passion and burning loins drove her forwards with a speed unheard of in a tortoise of her size. The sharks had not yet noticed Paul's presence. But as she hurried past them, the biggest one opened its mouth, bared its teeth, and said "Hello, Paul." Paul couldn't believe it! Finally, she was reunited.
